'''David Miln Smith''' (born October 17, 1938) is a speaker and adventure athlete.  He was the first man to swim from [[Africa]] to [[Europe]] across the [[Strait of Gibraltar]], which he did twice, first in 1966, and again in 1967.  He made a name for himself in the 1960s and 1970s with a series of extreme and international multi-sports events, such as "Everyman's Olympics" and the "Peace Pentathlon."  The latter got him on the cover of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' in 1970, where he was dubbed "Super Hippie."  Throughout the next few decades, he wrote books on [[yoga]] and health, and was the recurrent guest adventurer on television shows such as [[Johnny Carson]]'s ''[[The Tonight Show|Tonight Show]].''  Johnny Carson said, “He travels around the world doing all the things you want to do.”  The [[Today (NBC program)|Today Show]] called him "the King of the Risk Takers".

== Early life ==

David was the son of Dr. Seymour and Gladys Smith of [[San Francisco, California]].  He achieved [[Eagle Scout (Boy Scouts of America)|Eagle Scout]] at the age of 12 and a half, and was at the time the youngest known Eagle Scout.

== Later work ==

From 1973 to 1999 he was on staff at Earth House,<ref>[http://www.earthhouse.org Earth House website]</ref> a residential treatment center for young people diagnosed with [[schizophrenia]] and [[bipolar disorder]] in [[East Millstone, New Jersey]], first as a [[yoga]] instructor and [[psychodrama]] [[facilitator]], and later as the director of their "Earth Adventure" program, an early example of [[wilderness therapy]] in which a group of twenty to forty patients would be led on a camping expedition onto the [[Appalachian Trail]], and perform a wilderness course including [[Rock climbing|climbing]], [[Abseiling|rappelling]], and [[canoeing]] through [[rapids]].

From 1990 to the present, he has been on staff as the motivational speaker for the Northern California Service League,<ref>[http://www.norcalserviceleague.org Northern California Service League website]</ref> giving talks twice a month to [[Parole|ex-cons]] in [[San Quentin State Prison|San Quentin]], the maximum security prison, [[Jails of San Francisco, California|San Bruno Jail]], San Francisco Jail, and at the center.  He urges them to "get a job, not do a job."

He is also on the available-speaker lists of several agencies which arrange speakers for special occasions.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.wowspeakers.com/speakers/bio.cfm?speakerID=smit0154 |title=David M. Smith |access-date=2011-03-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718115334/http://www.wowspeakers.com/speakers/bio.cfm?speakerID=smit0154 |archive-date=2011-07-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
